ESP32_DevKitC.notes: Standard 30-pin ESP32 DevKitC / DevKit V1 layout. GPIO34-39 are input-only (no internal pull-up/down, cannot be used for output).

M5Stack_Core2.notes: M5Stack Core2 has an internal I2C bus for onboard peripherals (AXP192 power IC, touch controller) and a Port A (Grove connector) for external I2C sensors.
M5Stack_Core2.note_on_shared_bus: Internal I2C (power/touch) is on GPIO21/GPIO22 -- do not reuse these for external devices. Use Port A (GPIO32/33) for external I2C sensors instead.

Raspberry_Pi_40pin.notes: Applies to Raspberry Pi 3/4/5 and Zero with the standard 40-pin header. BCM numbering shown (what most Python GPIO libraries use), not physical pin numbers.
Raspberry_Pi_40pin.important_voltage_note: Raspberry Pi GPIO pins are 3.3V ONLY. Never connect a 5V logic sensor output directly to a GPIO pin -- use a level shifter or voltage divider, or this will damage the Pi.

Raspberry_Pi_Pico_RP2040.notes: IMPORTANT: this is a DIFFERENT product from 'Raspberry_Pi_40pin' above. The Pico is a bare microcontroller board (RP2040 chip) with NO operating system -- it runs MicroPython or C/C++ SDK directly on the chip, NOT Linux. Code for this board uses MicroPython's `machine` module (machine.Pin, machine.I2C, etc.), never RPi.GPIO, never smbus, and never assumes a filesystem, terminal, or OS services beyond what MicroPython itself provides.
Raspberry_Pi_Pico_RP2040.power_note: 3V3 OUT pin (pin 36) provides regulated 3.3V; VSYS (pin 39) accepts 1.8-5.5V input; VBUS (pin 40) is 5V from USB
Raspberry_Pi_Pico_RP2040.onboard_led: GP25 (or 'LED' by name on some MicroPython builds)
Raspberry_Pi_Pico_RP2040.gpio_voltage: 3.3V logic ONLY -- same 5V-tolerance caution as ESP32 applies

Arduino_Uno.notes: ATmega328P-based, 5V logic (unlike ESP32/Pico's 3.3V) -- most 3.3V-only modules (NRF24L01, some SPI radios) need a level shifter here. Only 2KB SRAM total, so avoid heavy libraries/large buffers. Only ONE hardware UART (shared with USB programming) and ONE I2C bus.

ESP8266_NodeMCU.notes: IMPORTANT PITFALL: NodeMCU board silkscreen 'D' labels do NOT match the underlying GPIO numbers used in code -- e.g. silkscreen D1 is actually GPIO5, D2 is GPIO4, D3 is GPIO0, D4 is GPIO2. Always use the silkscreen D-number in Arduino code (D1, D2, etc.), not the raw GPIO number, since the board variant file maps them. Only ONE analog input (A0), limited to 0-1.0V range on bare ESP8266 (NodeMCU boards typically add a divider bringing it to 0-3.3V -- check your specific board).
ESP8266_NodeMCU.onboard_led: D4 (GPIO2, inverted logic -- LOW turns it on)
avoid_pins: D3/D4/D8 are boot-mode strapping pins, avoid for general I/O if possible

Teensy_4_0.notes: ARM Cortex-M7 @600MHz via Teensyduino (Arduino-compatible). 3.3V logic, but most digital pins ARE 5V tolerant (check pinout diagram for exceptions). Has a built-in microSD slot on some carrier boards. Native CAN bus support (FlexCAN) unlike most Arduino-class boards.

power.VIN: 5V input via USB or VIN pin

Teensy_4_0.pwm_capable_pins: most digital pins support PWM (check pinout diagram for exact list)
Teensy_4_0.can_bus: CAN pins vary by revision -- check specific Teensy 4.0 pinout diagram

pins.DIO0: any free GPIO, must support interrupts

pins.DATA: any free GPIO, needs 10k pull-up resistor to VCC
any free GPIO, needs 4.7k pull-up resistor to VCC
